wheel.note: Japan-market Jimny 1000/1300 used 6 bolts on the same 139.7 mm circle

max_tire.note: Zukiworld owners: 215/75R15 fits with no modifications; 225s with a little effort.
Needs trimming or a 1.5–2 in lift; flatten the inner fender seams. Trail Tough rates its 2 in Old Man Emu kit as right for 29 in tires.
Trail Tough's deluxe SPOA kit is rated for up to 31 in tires, with knuckle-over steering.

items.title: Front seat belt buckle release buttons can break
items.summary: The red 'PRESS' release buttons can break and jam the buckle; dealers replaced or repaired buckles free of charge.

timeline.change: SJ410 (Jimny 1000 in Japan from 1982) replaces the LJ80: F10A 1.0 four, four-speed, drum brakes
SJ413 / Jimny 1300 (JA51): G13A 1.3, five-speed, front discs, anti-roll bar, new dash and grille
Santana starts building SJs in Spain (March); Maruti Gypsy launches in India (December); US Samurai goes on sale in California in November as a 1986 model
'1988½' US update: softer springs, revised shocks, thicker front anti-roll bar, 0.865 fifth gear, new grille, gauges and seats. In July, Consumer Reports rates it 'Not Acceptable'
US Samurai gets throttle-body fuel injection (MotorTrend)
US rear seat deleted for 1994–95 rather than add rear shoulder belts
Last US model year; coil-sprung JB32 launched in Japan in November
Japanese production ends; replaced by the JB23 Jimny. Santana and Maruti carry on

identify.intro: Samurais are widely modified, and Santana, Maruti and Japanese versions share the basic design with many detail differences. Confirm what you're looking at.

items.head: Carbureted or injected
items.body: AMSOIL's capacity lookups list 1986–89 US Samurais with engine code 5 and 1990–95 with engine code 3. A US truck with an automatic gearbox is a swap.

items.head: Early or '1988½'
items.body: The 1988½ update brought a new grille and wheels, new gauges and seats. Transfer case fill and drain plugs differ between 1986–88 and 1988.5–95 trucks, and the 1986–89 master cylinder is specific.

items.head: Narrow or wide track
items.body: The wide-track Samurai measures 1,300 mm front and 1,310 mm rear (1986 US brochure). Narrow SJ410/413 trucks are about 1,210 / 1,220 mm.

items.head: Indian-built trucks
items.body: Australian Sierra Stockman utes sourced from India in the 1990s carry an MG410 badge on the front fenders and a VIN starting with MA (Wikipedia).

values.intro: Samurai prices have climbed from throwaway to collectible. Low-mileage stock trucks and well-built engine-swapped trucks bring the most.
values.note: Based on 22 Bring a Trailer sales from September 2025 to October 2026: $5,500 to $25,000, median about $9,400. A 7k-mile 1987 sold for $24,000 and a 1.6 16V-powered 1987 for $25,000.
